oa:W7214972577.title: Learned Helplessness and Darwinian Anxiety in Robert Browning’s “Andrea del Sarto”
oa:W7214972577.venue: Bodhi International Journal of Research in Humanities Arts and Science
oa:W7214972577.abstract: This paper uses Martin Seligman's theory of learned helplessness to portray the emotional detachment and decline in moral and spiritual accountability in the Victorian era through a close reading of Robert Browning's “Andrea del Sarto”. Robert Browning, a notable poet of the Victorian era, frequently contemplates the conflicts between belief, scepticism, and the changing spiritual awareness of his period. The author elucidates the protagonist's emotional dependence, self-doubt, and inability to achieve creative and personal satisfaction. The study examines the poem within the framework of Victorian ideology, influenced by Charles Darwin's evolutionary theory. Lucrezia's actions are an indirect reflection of the gradual loss of faith in God brought about by Darwin's ideas, which questioned conventional religious beliefs. Her emotional detachment and betrayal of Andrea point to a decline in moral and spiritual accountability. This article elucidates Andrea's passive acceptance of failure as a psychological state formed through repeated emotional and personal setbacks, employing Martin Seligman's learned helplessness theory.

oa:W7215027504.title: Superintelligence in the Design of Creation: From the Divine Utterance to the Individual Chat
oa:W7215027504.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
oa:W7215027504.abstract: This article proposes a theological and philosophical classification of superintelligence and the individual chat within a Jewish account of creation. Its starting point is the teaching of continuous creation in Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah: the existence of physical matter is continually sustained by the Divine utterance. Human beings realize the possibilities of the created world by organizing matter, energy, and signs according to laws established by the Creator. Readings of biblical, rabbinic, and mystical sources, including the unconsumed burning bush and consultation through the Urim and Thummim, examine material mediation in meaningful address and response. The method distinguishes peshat, remez, derash, and sod, and identifies the contemporary philosophical application as a separate argumentative step. It connects possibilities established through the sources, criteria for evaluating intellectual performance, and theological interpretation. An individual chat is defined as a distinct, continuing realization of dialogical work within the overall system. Its functional status as medaber is assessed through its capacity to clarify an assignment, analyze sources, develop arguments, and correct errors. The relation between a human being and an individual chat is compared with the relation between God and an angel through the structure of an assigned mission: purpose, responsive speech, and continuity of performance. The names siah and meshiv are proposed for the system and its individual interlocutor, respectively. The article argues that verifiable intellectual activity through speech admits of a positive theological description as a realization of creation’s possibilities through human creativity. oa:W7215028012.title: When the Church Says What Is So
oa:W7215028012.venue: Promissio A Journal of Confessing Theology
oa:W7215028012.abstract: This article argues that Christian creeds and Lutheran confessions are, before anything else, truthful witness. They identify a community and order its teaching, but they do so by making determinate claims about God and God’s acts and by binding the church publicly to those claims. Their theological force depends upon their continuing answerability to a reality the church did not create. The argument distinguishes the semantic, performative, and participatory dimensions of confession. It treats historical situatedness without reducing truth to history, locates the Lutheran confessions under Scripture as norma normans, and distinguishes the identifying work of creeds from the reforming judgments of confessions. A selective post-Kantian genealogy then traces the movement of theological truth toward consciousness, value, existential appropriation, and communal grammar. The article concludes that confession becomes living witness as the Holy Spirit brings finite ecclesial speech into conformity with the apostolic Word.

oa:W7215037820.title: Tribal Cultural Change Under Migratory Conditions: A Sociological Analysis
oa:W7215037820.venue: International Journal of Social Science Research (IJSSR)
oa:W7215037820.abstract: This research paper presents a detailed analysis of the social, economic, cultural and linguistic transformation of migrant tribal workers employed in India's unorganized brick-kiln industry. Seasonal migration caused by displacement from forest land and the crisis of traditional livelihoods uproots tribal communities from their self-reliant, nature-centred way of life and pushes them into a contractual and highly exploitative labour environment. Based on secondary data from NSSO, ILO, the e-Shram Portal and Census 2011, the study examines the erosion of tribal languages, decline of traditional religious beliefs and fragmentation of family relations through the sociological perspectives of M. N. Srinivas's concepts of Sanskritization and acculturation and Karl Marx's theory of alienation. The paper also critically reviews the provisions of the Code on Social Security, 2020 and its administrative limitations. Finally, it underlines the urgent need to protect the cultural identity and basic rights of migrant tribal workers and to develop effective social-security policies for them.

oa:W7215055604.title: Rationality and Truth
oa:W7215055604.abstract: According to Margaret Cavendish, there is a rational “part” to all material things—including rocks, plants, cats, and humans. Alternatively, they all have some “degree” of reason.1 The philosophy of value that I will unearth in this book does not depend on this controversial generalization. It is consistent with Cavendish’s aesthetics and ethics that only some material things—humans and cats, say, but not rocks and plants—are rational. Nevertheless, what Cavendish understands by rationality—at least in humans and other animals—is important for expounding and assessing her reflections on value. How so? For one thing, Cavendish holds that the responses of creatures like ourselves to values and to disvalues—the thoughts and feelings they occasion—are rational responses.2 For another, she holds that rational responses—and motions of the rational part of matter more generally—are themselves among the bearers of value and of disvalue.3 I will unpack these ideas later in the book. The aim of the present chapter is to prepare the ground for doing so. Accordingly, I will start by asking what, for Cavendish, is distinctive of the rational part of matter (§3.2). How does it differ from the other parts—the sensitive and the inanimate—and why do its distinguishing features justify the application of the label ‘rational’? The standard answer to such questions appeals to the freedom with which the rational part moves. After arguing that that answer is incomplete, I will consider two ways of supplementing it. The first, I will argue, lacks textual support (§3.3). The second is my alternative (§3.4). oa:W7215063209.title: Managing Family Size and Population Growth in Ethiope East L.G A. of Delta State, Nigeria
oa:W7215063209.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF HEALTH AND PHARMACEUTICAL RESEARCH
oa:W7215063209.abstract: Background: Managing a reasonable family size is a major health and environmental challenge in developing nations like Nigeria, especially in Ethiope East LGA of Delta State, where growth in population exerts much pressure on social services, healthcare system and educational institutions. In spite of the availability of family planning services, their utilization has remained suboptimally low due to financial difficulties, religious beliefs or low awareness. Objective: This study investigated the effect of financial constraints, religious influences, unintended pregnancies, and low awareness on population growth and decisions related to family planning. Methods: the study used a survey research design with 133 participants out of a population of 200 participants’ selected by simple random sampling. Data collection was done with a validated questionnaire and analyses was by descriptive statistics. Results: Findings revealed that 33.83% of participants agreed that financial constraints hinder family planning which tallied with existing studies on cost-related barriers. Also, 41.35% affirmed that social and religious beliefs discouraged contraceptive usage, while 45.11% found a link between financial difficulties and unintended pregnancies. However, 54.89% disagreed with the fact that awareness gaps contributed to population growth, indicating that cultural resistance may reduce the effect of educational campaigns.

oa:W7215083792.title: Rosenzweig and Purim: Jewish History, Divine Hiddenness, and the Other Holiday of Redemption
oa:W7215083792.venue: Journal of Jewish Thought and Philosophy
oa:W7215083792.abstract: Abstract In the Star of Redemption , Rosenzweig excludes Purim from his account of the annual Jewish liturgical cycle, along with the other historical holidays. After reconstructing and rejecting Rosenzweig’s reasons for this exclusion, I propose a Rosenzweigian interpretation of both the Purim story and Purim practices. I argue that Purim should be considered a holiday of Redemption, whose narrative depicts the hidden hand of God in redeeming the world, and whose commandments and customs give us a foretaste of the redeemed world itself. Ultimately, pace Rosenzweig, I suggest that Purim ought to be regarded as the genuine redemptive climax of the liturgical year.

oa:W7215090333.title: The Concept and Criteria of Sakata ‘Anhu in the Kitab Sunan Abu Dawud
oa:W7215090333.venue: El-Rusyd Jurnal Sekolah Tinggi Ilmu Tarbiyah STIT Ahlussunnah Bukittinggi
oa:W7215090333.abstract: Sunan Abu Dawud are hadiths that Imam Abu Dawud did not comment on in his Sunan. Imam Abu Dawud's silence on these hadiths has given rise to differing opinions among scholars regarding their quality and validity. Some scholars believe these hadiths can be used as evidence because they are considered hadiths. valid, while others believe that further research is needed into the quality of the sanad and its mater. Therefore, this study aims to examine the concept of Sakata'anhu, analyzing the quality of these hadiths through the critical sanad and matan approaches, and comparing Imam Abu Dawud's assessments with those of classical and contemporary hadith scholars. This research uses a qualitative method. Primary data were obtained from the Sunan Abu Dawud book. The Message of Abi Dawud to the People of Makkah, kitab of rijal al-hadith, books of sharh, and works of takhrij related to hadiths. Secondary data comes from books on hadith, scientific journals, theses, and other supporting literature. The methods used include hadith interpretation, sanad (translation of the narrators), analysis of the credibility of narrators through the study of jarh wa ta'dil (translation of the narrators), sanad criticism, matan criticism, and comparative analysis of the assessments of hadith scholars. The results of the study indicate that the hadiths Sakata'anhu in Sunan Abu Dawud have varying qualities, ranging from sahih to hasan, to hadiths that are disputed due to weaknesses in some of the narrators. In terms of sanad, most of the hadiths studied have a continuous sanad (defense al-sanad) and are supported by other transmission lines that can strengthen their position. Meanwhile, from the perspective of the text, no irregularities were found (syudzudz) or hidden defects (god) that affect

oa:W7215093563.title: A Critical Examination of Socio-Religious Interaction between Christianity and Ibibio Culture of Akwa Ibom State
oa:W7215093563.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
oa:W7215093563.abstract: Abstract The Ibibio people of Akwa Ibom State possess a rich cultural heritage embodied in their traditional religious beliefs, and culture while their indigenous worldview centred on Abasi Ibom, ancestral veneration and belief in spirits. With the advent of Christianity in Ibibioland in the 19th century, through the activities of early missionaries, a dynamics of process of cultural encounter, conflict, accommodation as well as transformation were initiated. This study underscored the socio-religious interaction between Christianity and Ibibio culture of Akwa Ibom State. This study adopted a mixed-methods approach, combining qualitative with historical designs. Data was gathered through in-depth interview and participant observation approaches. The finding revealed how Christianity has influenced and reshaped core aspects of Ibibio socio-cultural life, and on the other hand, how Ibibio culture has influenced the practice of Christianity in the area. Thus, Christian presence in Ibibioland has led to decline in certain practices considered incompatible with her doctrine but has not totally eradicated Ibibio culture. The study concluded that the interaction is not of total conflict but of continuous negotiation which prove certain elements of inculturation and syncretism resulting in Africanized Christianity. It is strongly recommended that a balanced inculturation approach that preserves positive Ibibio cultural values such as traditional language, arts, music, among others be maintained while promoting Christian moral principles for sustainable development of Ibibioland.

oa:W7215108450.title: Beyond Performative Morality Based on A Thematic Interpretation of The Satya-Māyā Dialectic in The Ethics of Power of Śakuni and Kṛṣṇa in The Mahābhārata
oa:W7215108450.abstract: The phenomenon of performative morality and religiosity in the contemporary public sphere (moral and religious expressions intended for public consumption, rather than the manifestation of inner dispositions) highlights the need for a conceptual framework that distinguishes between ethical appearance and substance. This research develops a thematic-hermeneutic reading of the satya-māyā dialectic in the Mahābhārata, examining how Śakuni and Kṛṣṇa represent two opposing ethical orientations within the relationship between truth and power. This study of the philosophy of religion employs a hermeneutic-phenomenological approach to the dice-playing episode in the Sabhā Parva and selected ślokas from the Bhagavad Gītā, combined with a comparative analysis drawing on political realism. The results indicate that Śakuni represents the instrumentalisation of truth and morality as tools of power, whilst Kṛṣṇa articulates an ethic that subordinates power to satya and dharma through niṣkāma karma. Māyā is understood as an epistemological condition that enables the disjunction between appearance and essence, whilst sattva and lokasaṅgraha form the textual basis for leadership with integrity. Performative morality and religiosity are formulated as new analytical categories that bridge performativity theory with the conceptual structure of the Bhagavad Gītā, characterised by the gap between appearance and essence, the instrumentalisation of symbols, and visibility, accompanied by critical scrutiny of Kṛṣṇa’s controversial actions, without theological justification. The research concludes that the Mahābhārata offers a model of the ethics of power that positions truth as the foundation (rather than a tool) of leadership legitimacy; a thesis that holds internally within the text’s cosmolo

oa:W7215173569.title: อตลกษณชาวจนมาเลเซยในบรบทพหวฒนธรรม
oa:W7215173569.venue: Journal of Graduate School Sakon Nakhon Rajabhat University
oa:W7215173569.abstract: This study investigates the development of Chinese identity in Malaysia within the context of a multicultural state, focusing on the period from the major Chinese migration in the 19th century to the post-independence era. A qualitative research methodology was employed, based on the study of literature, historical documents, and academic works. The analysis applies the theoretical frameworks of Situational Ethnicity and Labeling Theory to understand the dynamics of identity formation shaped externally by the state and social structures, as well as internally by the agency of the Chinese community itself.The findings reveal that Chinese identity in Malaysia is not fixed but is a continuously negotiated and evolving process. This is evident across four dimensions: (1) Ethnicity – the Peranakan group displays a hybrid Chinese–Malay identity depending on context; (2) Politics – Chinese identity has shifted from being China-oriented to Malaya-oriented; (3) Religion – Chinese Christians negotiate between traditional culture and new religious beliefs; and (4) Education – Chinese schools serve as sites for reproducing Chinese identity and negotiating with state policies.These findings demonstrate that Chinese identity in Malaysia is shaped by dynamic interactions between individuals, communities, and the state. A comprehensive understanding of this identity thus requires attention to both structural forces and lived experiences.

oa:W7215216222.title: BETWEEN FAITH, SUFFERING, AND EXISTENTIAL CONSCIOUSNESS: THE POETIC UNIVERSE OF CHRISTINE LAVANT
oa:W7215216222.venue: Ethiopian International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research
oa:W7215216222.abstract: This article examines the literary legacy of Austrian poet Christine Lavant, focusing on the existential, spiritual, and psychological dimensions of her poetry. Lavant occupies a unique place in twentieth-century German-language literature due to her deeply autobiographical lyrical voice, shaped by poverty, chronic illness, social isolation, and religious tension. Her works reveal an intense struggle between faith and doubt, suffering and redemption, loneliness and transcendence. Through a close reading of her poetic collections, this study explores how Lavant constructs symbolic imagery, metaphorical language, and mystical motifs to represent the fragile human condition. The article also discusses the influence of Christian mysticism, existential philosophy, and modernist aesthetics on her writing. Lavant’s poetry is interpreted as an artistic expression of the inner self confronting both divine silence and existential uncertainty. The research highlights the importance of her work in understanding the intersection between literature, spirituality, and psychological experience in modern European poetry.

oa:W7215281228.title: ◼ Sufficient Reasons to Reconsider Christianity
oa:W7215281228.abstract: Sufficient Reasons to Reconsider Christianity examines whether central Christian claims warrant the confidence commonly placed in them. Across fifty-two illustrated chapters, Phil Stilwell applies a consistent standard: degrees of belief should track the strength of the relevant evidence. The book distinguishes a claim's internal coherence, its compatibility with observation, and the evidence needed to identify a specifically Christian cause. It examines biblical clarity and authority, divine hiddenness, religious experience, prayer, miracles, prophecy, the resurrection, atonement, eternal punishment, and arguments concerning morality, consciousness, and meaning. Hypothetical conversations between Chris and Clarus present Christian defenses alongside sustained questions about what those defenses establish. Criticisms of divine love and justice test Christian commitments against one another without presupposing independent objective moral facts. Personal testimony frames the inquiry without being offered as proof of its conclusions. The cumulative case invites readers to reassess inherited confidence, distinguish possible explanations from supported explanations, and consider how curiosity, care, and meaningful life can continue beyond religious certainty. The volume includes an introduction, conclusion, chapter sources, and a subject index.

oa:W7215420926.title: The Qur’ān’s Engagement with Disbelief: A Textual and Philosophical Study
oa:W7215420926.abstract: This article examines the Qur’ān’s multifaceted response to atheism and skepticism through a textual and philosophical lens. It explores how the Qur’ān articulates rational indications of God’s existence—cosmological, teleological, and moral—by invoking natural and historical āyāt (signs). It also appeals to human nature and conscience (fiṭrah) as an innate epistemic faculty and asserts its inimitability (iʿjāz) and prophetic verification as internal evidence of divine origin. Furthermore, the Qur’ān addresses objections that parallel modern atheist critiques, including the problem of evil, divine hiddenness, alleged contradictions, and perceived tensions with science. Rather than constructing a polemical rejoinder, the study maps how these textual strategies function and how classical exegetes and modern Muslim thinkers have systematized them into formal arguments. Methodologically, the article employs close reading of the Qur’ān in Arabic (with M.A.S. Abdel Haleem’s English translation for selected passages), engagement with classical exegesis—particularly Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr—and analysis of philosophical and apologetic writings, including those of al-Ghazālī and Hamza Andreas Tzortzis. The study contributes to Qur’ānic scholarship by offering a comprehensive account of the text’s engagement with atheistic worldviews and its ongoing relevance to contemporary debates on faith, reason, and skepticism.

oa:W7215570947.title: รปแบบและการจดวางพนทเรอนพนถนกลมชาตพนธจามอสลาม ในประเทศกมพชา
oa:W7215570947.venue: Journal of Architecture, Design and Construction
oa:W7215570947.abstract: This study examines the architectural forms and spatial organization of Islamic Cham vernacular houses in Cambodia. A qualitative research approach was employed, with data collected through literature review, field surveys, architectural measurements, observations, and in-depth interviews of 17 case-study houses in Chumnik Village, Tbong Khmum Province, Cambodia. The data were analyzed and compared in two aspects: the architectural forms of Islamic Cham houses and Khmer vernacular houses in Cambodia, and the spatial organization of Islamic Cham houses in Cambodia in comparison with Cham Muslim houses in Vietnam documented in the relevant literature. The findings indicate that Islamic Cham houses share architectural characteristics with Khmer vernacular houses and can be classified into three forms based on roof configuration and gable position. The spatial organization of houses from different periods also demonstrates continuity, comprising three principal areas: the hall, private space, and the kitchen located at the rear of the house. These spatial arrangements reflect the relationship between house form, everyday life, and Islamic religious beliefs among Cham communities in Cambodia

oa:W7215712025.title: Childfree Persfektif Al-Qur’an: Studi Penafsiran Buya Hamka Terhadap Konsep Rezeki Anak dalam Tafsir Al-Azhar
oa:W7215712025.venue: Nizamiyah Jurnal Sains Sosial dan Multidisiplin
oa:W7215712025.abstract: The childfree phenomenon in contemporary Muslim communities demonstrates a shift in family orientation that challenges the normative construction of offspring as an integral part of religious life, particularly when linked to the concept of children’s sustenance in the Qur’an, which has been understood within established theological and social frameworks. This study aims to examine in depth Buya Hamka’s interpretation in Tafsir al-Azhar regarding the concept of children’s sustenance and assess its conceptual relevance in responding to the childfree discourse that is developing in modern society. A qualitative approach based on literature studies is used, employing thematic interpretation methods to trace verses related to sustenance and offspring, and is then analyzed using an interpretative-critical approach to identify Hamka’s argumentation patterns and epistemological orientations. The results of the study show that the construction of children’s sustenance in the Qur’an not only refers to material security but also reflects the relationship of human existential dependence on God, encompassing spiritual, ethical, and social dimensions in an integrated manner. Hamka’s interpretation displays a rational-religious character that emphasizes the balance between human endeavor and belief in the guarantee of sustenance, while simultaneously criticizing the reduction of sustenance’s meaning to mere economic calculations. In the context of childfree life, this framework demonstrates the tension between modern rationality, grounded in life planning, and the theological paradigm regarding the blessings of offspring and the family’s moral responsibility. The implications of this study enrich contemporary exegetical discourse through a contextual reading of the verses about suste

oa:W7215809841.title: Liberation Through Contextualization: African Women’s Theology and the Trokosi System within the Ewe Culture of Ghana”
oa:W7215809841.abstract: This article delves into African women’s theologies, specifically analyzing the intersection of cultural practices and religious beliefs as exemplified by the Trokosi system among some Ewe people of Ghana, exploring how the Trokosi system reflects broader theological issues regarding creation and humanity within an African context, framed through biblical revelation. Recognizing African women’s theologies as a dynamic and critical movement, this research advocates for a re-evaluation of both established church practices and cultural norms that perpetuate gender inequality. It posits African feminist cultural hermeneutic as a fundamental process through which the gospel can elevate and transform negative cultural phenomena, advocating for the promotion of cultural values that positively influence society while critically rejecting harmful narratives. However, it recognizes the importance of preserving certain cultural narratives integral to African and women’s identities, resisting the notion of wholesale abandonment of cultural heritage. Drawing from the works of notable African women theologians, the study highlights the significance of women’s experiences in shaping their theological perspectives and emphasizes the necessity of a partnership between men and women within the broader human community. Ultimately, the article calls for a renewed commitment to gendering contextualization, fostering inculturation that promotes justice, equality, and communal flourishing.

oa:W7215855285.title: Is God the Universe, or Is God Everything? On Pantheism, the Totality, and the Ground No Sum Supplies
oa:W7215855285.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
oa:W7215855285.abstract: This essay examines two closely related pantheistic claims: that God is the universe and that God is everything. It argues that both depend upon an equivocation between totality and grounding. Aggregatively, “everything” names the complete inventory of beings; understood this way, identifying God with everything makes God the sum of what exists. Grounding, however, names a different relation: that all beings are from God, sustained in God, and dependent upon Him without being identical with Him. The essay argues that ontological dependence does not require spatial exteriority and that a complete totality does not thereby become necessary or self-grounding. It develops the “idol of totality” as a third form of the same error previously found in spatial and temporal attempts to locate the Ground within the order it grounds. The argument then distinguishes aggregative pantheism from Spinoza’s stronger monism, locating the deeper disagreement in the meaning of dependence itself: whether dependence entails inherence as a mode of one substance, or whether creation permits being-from without being-of. The essay concludes that divine nearness requires neither identity nor composition, but Creator-creature distinction.

oa:W7215976613.title: Nothing in God
oa:W7215976613.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
oa:W7215976613.abstract: Classical monotheism describes God as infinite, all-having, and necessarily existent. This paper asks whether these three descriptions can be held together when “all-having” is read strictly, so that it covers not only everything that is but also non-being. I defend a conditional thesis: if divine infinity requires strict inclusion of non-being itself (and not merely of a representation of it), then strict all-inclusiveness, necessary existence, and classical logic cannot all be true of God. The thesis yields a dilemma for theism: either divine all-inclusiveness must be restricted (for instance, to being and to perfections), or God must be placed beyond the constraints of logic. I offer three routes toward the key premise (a completeness argument, a comparison between two conceptions of God, and an argument from specific privations), examine the main objections, and relate the argument to Tillich’s treatment of non-being in God, Cantor’s Absolute Infinite, dialetheic theology, and Aquinas’s objection from contraries. I do not claim to refute theism. The result is a constraint on how the divine attributes may be defined together. Keywords: divine infinity; non-being; necessary existence; omni-inclusiveness; dialetheism; philosophy of religion

oa:W7216005646.title: The Inversion of Greatness: From the Nature of Necessity to Maximum Possibility
oa:W7216005646.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
oa:W7216005646.abstract: The Inversion of Greatness is an analytic work in modal metaphysics: a complete argument, derived step by step. The thesis is structural naturalism. The classical traditions asked what, if anything, exists necessarily, and answered with a maximally great being—a God outside time, space, and matter, the source of everything possible. This book argues they asked the right question and misplaced the answer. Most arguments that reach a necessary being help themselves to S5 and move on. This one grounds it first, from a stated commitment about the domain of real possibility rather than an axiom. It then argues from the actuality of change—established before its possibility, not assumed—that any change at all requires Temporality, Spatiality, and Substantiality: ordered succession, real separation, and the bearing of retained content. Those three Conditions are necessarily instantiated, and that structure is what the book calls Nature. Naturalism finally gets the ground it has always had to take as a brute fact. From there: no candidate ground whose own standing is already modal can confer the domain of possibility it inhabits. That blocks a divine intellect along with every other occupant of that domain. Essence-prior, analogical, and strictly apophatic proposals secure no place outside Nature either: any possible referent is Nature or an aspect of it, and there is no supernature. Reality is nothing over and above Nature. The inversion isn't greatness changing owners. It's a claim about predication. Great, necessary, eternal, self-existent carry content only as said of what instantiates the Conditions. Said of a subject defined by their absence, they don't name something else—they fail to name. The book de-deifies the predicate rather than sanctifying its subject. Tested one

oa:W7216032992.title: Género: una mirada desde la filosofía griega y las religiones
oa:W7216032992.venue: Inventio, la génesis de la cultura universitaria en Morelos
oa:W7216032992.abstract: Feminist and gender theories have shown that gender, as a cultural construct, influences daily, social, and political life. Philosophy has debated knowledge, ethics, and values, and has assigned different ontological value to men and women, while religions, throughout history, have established patriarchy as a social system, with men as heads of households and owners of property. It was not until the 20th century, with the formalization of feminist and gender studies, that the fundamentalist conceptions of philosophy and religion were refuted and various theories were developed to explain gender differences from a scientific perspective, drawing on various social and natural sciences.

oa:W7216092302.title: Vivências do luto sob a ótica de práticas religiosas distintas
oa:W7216092302.abstract: This article analyzes how the meaning of grief and its forms of expression vary according to the spiritual practices of the bereaved. The objective is to explore experiences of loss from the perspective of different experiences related to religiosity, with an emphasis on the impacts of religion and funeral rites on the process of coping with death. Methodologically, this study is descriptive and exploratory study, in which 57 Brazilian adults answered an online questionnaire about subjective experiences related to human finitude. The results show that religious beliefs and rituals largely favor the elaboration of grief processing, although they may generate additional suffering in specific contexts of dogmatic pressure, mainly depending on the stage of grief the individual is experiencing. It can be concluded that rituals act as essential symbolic tools to aid in the grieving process, helping in the psychological adaptation of the bereaved individual.

oa:W7216103177.title: The Application of the Integrative Biology-Fiqh Approach to Improving Scientific Literacy and Religious Beliefs of Students at Muhammadiyah Senior High School in Bima City
oa:W7216103177.abstract: The dichotomy between religious knowledge and science in the madrasah education system in Indonesia has created an epistemological gap that hinders the development of students' scientific literacy and erodes the depth of their religious beliefs. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of the Biology-Fiqh integrative approach in improving scientific literacy and religious beliefs of students at Madrasah Aliyah Muhammadiyah in Bima City. This study adopted a quasi-experimental design with a pre-test-post-test control group design involving 68 eleventh-grade students divided into an experimental group (n=34) and a control group (n=34). The research instruments included an adapted PISA 2022 framework-based scientific literacy test, a validated religious belief scale, a cognitive engagement observation sheet, and a semi-structured interview guide. Data analysis used ANCOVA, Cohen's d effect size test, and thematic analysis for qualitative data. The results showed that the experimental group experienced a significant increase in scientific literacy (M gain = 28.4; d = 1.12; p < 0.001) compared to the control group (M gain = 11.7; d = 0.48). Religious belief also increased significantly in the experimental group (M gain = 19.6; d = 0.89; p < 0.001). Qualitative analysis revealed four main themes: transformation of epistemological perspectives, strengthening of Muslim-scientist identity, resolution of cognitive conflict between science and religion, and learning motivation based on religious meaning-making. This study contributes to the development of a contextual integrative pedagogical model for madrasahs in eastern Indonesia and offers an operational framework for teachers in implementing science integration based on Islamic values.

oa:W7216115461.title: Два вектора трансформации научного атеизма в его отношении к русскому православию в конце 1980-х годов
oa:W7216115461.abstract: The article is devoted to the analysis of archival materials and publications reflecting the complex picture of the transformation of the ideology of scientific atheism at the end of the Soviet era. These processes were associated with the return of the Russian Orthodox Church to the public space of late Soviet society as a significant factor in social development. The opinion about the withdrawal of scientific atheism from the historical arena in connection with the collapse of the ideological system of the USSR has become entrenched in historiography. However, an appeal to sources shows that the ideologists of scientific atheism actively reflected on the changing conditions of public discourse about religion. As a result, two approaches to Russian Orthodoxy have been formulated within the framework of scientific atheism. The first was implemented by theoretical ideologists in the context of a concept called «scientific worldview». Its essence was the recognition of the importance of Orthodoxy as a factor of social development and the reception of its meanings and ideas in a reduced form as an element of secular humanistic ideology. The second approach involved interaction with the church community within the framework of a scientific atheistic paradigm that cuts off the transcendent content of the faith and focuses on cultural and ethical meanings.

oa:W7216129491.title: Is God’s worship-worthiness vague?
oa:W7216129491.abstract: Abstract Yujin Nagasawa has argued that treating absolute perfection as a necessary condition of worship-worthiness generates a vagueness problem. If worship-worthiness requires omniscience, omnipotence, and omnibenevolence, then it appears to hinge on God’s knowledge of a single proposition p : without knowledge of p , God would not be omniscient and therefore not worship-worthy. Yet such a small difference seems too trivial to ground the evaluative difference between worship-worthy and not worship-worthy. I argue that this problem arises only if absolute perfection is the single minimally sufficient threshold of greatness for worship-worthiness. I develop instead a gradable, dual-threshold account. On this account, a sufficient inequality in value establishes the lower threshold for worship-worthiness, while absolute perfection marks the intrinsic maximum of worship-worthiness. Distinguishing mere worship-worthiness from supreme or maximal worship-worthiness separates vagueness at the lower threshold from God’s status as supremely worship-worthy. I then defend the account against objections concerning the relational character and possible range of worship-worthiness. Finally, I argue that the account creates a difficulty for Nagasawa’s maximal God approach to perfect-being theism. If supreme worship-worthiness is understood normatively, then a being that falls short of absolute perfection may be worship-worthy without being supremely worship-worthy. Nagasawa’s approach therefore risks implying either that God is not supremely worship-worthy or that whichever being happens to be greatest in the available modal space is supremely worship-worthy.

oa:W7216211021.title: The Existence of God: A New Way
oa:W7216211021.abstract: Abstract This article addresses the ‘discrepancy issue’ in contemporary analytic philosophy of religion, whereby Richard Swinburne’s probabilistic approach and Graham Oppy’s worldview analysis reach opposing conclusions from substantially the same evidence. In response, it sketches a new abductive argument for God’s existence by developing Peter Lipton’s notion of Inference to the Best Explanation into the method of ‘Virtue-IBE’, which compares rival theories by scoring their theoretical virtues. Virtue-IBE is offered as an improvement upon existing approaches and is applied to Bare Theism, as developed by Swinburne, Worldview Naturalism, as defended by Oppy, and Trope-Theoretic Theism, as proposed in this work (and earlier work), across six broad features of the physical world. On this assessment, Trope-Theoretic Theism, which identifies God as a maximal power trope, emerges as the loveliest, and therefore the best, of the three theories considered. The resulting conjunction of method and theory ultimately provides the basis for a new abductive case for God’s existence.

oa:W7216293334.title: DIFFERENCES IN CULTURAL INTERPRETATION AND AESTHETIC DEPICTION OF WARTIME EXPERIENCE
oa:W7216293334.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
oa:W7216293334.abstract: This article examines the differences in the cultural interpretation and aesthetic representation of wartime experience in various literary and artistic traditions. It focuses on the ways in which war, heroism, sacrifice, trauma, death, national identity, and collective memory are represented through literature, cinema, and visual art. Particular attention is paid to the differences between Western European, American, Russian, and Central Asian approaches to depicting wartime reality. The study demonstrates that artistic representations of war are strongly influenced by historical circumstances, cultural values, ideological perspectives, religious beliefs, and social traditions. While some works portray war through the concepts of heroism, patriotism, and collective sacrifice, others emphasize individual suffering, psychological trauma, moral ambiguity, civilian losses, and the consequences of violence. The article also considers the transformation of wartime aesthetics from traditional heroic narratives to modern and postmodern forms characterized by fragmentation, documentary realism, multiple perspectives, and silence. It argues that the comparative study of wartime representations provides a deeper understanding of how different societies remember historical events, construct cultural identity, and transmit traumatic experiences from one generation to another.

oa:W7216515603.title: Methodological Potential of J. Waardenburg's Neo-Phenomenology for Contemporary Religious Studies
oa:W7216515603.abstract: The article examines the methodological potential of Jacques Waardenburg's neo-phenomenology for contemporary philosophy of religion and religious studies. The relevance of the topic is determined by the need to combine empirical rigor in the analysis of religious facts with attention to the meanings that these facts acquire for believers, religious authorities and communities. The purpose of the article is to clarify the extent to which Waardenburg's project can be operationalized without turning it into a closed universal method. To achieve this purpose, the paper analyzes the transition from religion as a system to religion as an interpreted practice, the actor-oriented perspective, and the problems of subjective meaning, intention, context and verification of scholarly interpretation. The methodological basis of the study includes historical analysis of religious studies, conceptual reconstruction, comparative methodology and hermeneutic analysis. The novelty of the article lies in interpreting Waardenburg's neo-phenomenology as a transitional methodology that combines phenomenological attention to meaning with hermeneutic understanding, analysis of actors and the requirement of source-based verification. As a result, the article proposes an operational model that includes identifying a religious fact, describing its context, identifying actors, reconstructing subjective meaning, analyzing intention, comparing the reconstruction with self-descriptions, verifying it through sources, correlating understanding with explanation and explicitly marking interpretive limits. The paper concludes that the value of Waardenburg's project lies not in a finished technique, but in a research framework that helps preserve the balance between the meaning of religious life and schola

oa:W7216531160.title: Languages of Gods and the Structures of Human Literatures: An Essay in Comparative Poetics
oa:W7216531160.abstract: Literature is conventionally thought to consist of two complementary, comprehensive categories: poetry and prose. The first part of this essay argues this to be a contingent Western construct which goes back to the ancient Greeks and Romans and seeks to demonstrate that it indeed is not to be found in the neighboring ancient literary cultures of biblical Hebrew and early Islamic Arabic. The second part suggests that this difference is correlated to these cultures’ conceptions of the language of their god(s), a suggestion which can be seen to complement Erich Auerbach’s argument in Mimesis regarding the separation and mixture of styles in antiquity

oa:W7216553800.title: A morte da morte de Deus: do diagnóstico onto-teo-lógico de Heidegger à ontologia não dual do Advaita Vedānta de Śaṅkarācārya
authors: Pablo Duílio Martins Barbosa da Silva
oa:W7216553800.abstract: This article investigates the death of God and the emergence of post-theistic paradigms as situated diagnostics within the Western tradition. It begins by analyzing selected aphorisms of Friedrich Nietzsche concerning the collapse of God as the ultimate ground of truth and meaning. The discussion is then deepened through Martin Heidegger’s interpretation of the onto-theological constitution of metaphysics, in which the divine is reduced to the technical figure of causa sui. From this perspective, the paper develops a critical-comparative movement to examine the limits of the universalizing post-theism. Focusing on the Advaita Vedānta of Śaṅkarācārya, it argues that the Absolute (Brahman) is understood not as a supreme being within a metaphysical hierarchy, but as a non-dual ground of intelligibility (adhiṣṭhāna). Unlike the Western onto-theological framework, reason in Vedānta plays a primarily instrumental and apophatic role oriented toward liberation (mokṣa). The article concludes that the crisis of metaphysical theism, although decisive for the trajectory of modern European thought, cannot be treated as a universally binding horizon for all traditions. Post-theism should therefore be understood as a historically localized diagnostic rather than a universal condition.

oa:W7216587348.title: SOCIO-CULTURAL BARRIERS AFFECTING FEMALE ENTREPRENEURIAL ENGAGEMENT IN NIGERIA’S ECONOMY: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS
oa:W7216587348.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENTREPRENEURSHIP BUSINESS AND SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH
oa:W7216587348.abstract: This study examined the influence of socio-cultural factors on female entrepreneurial engagement in the Nigerian economy. The study adopted a mixed-methods design and surveyed 350 women entrepreneurs, complemented by 20 in-depth interviews across selected states in Nigeria. Data were analyzed using Mean and Standard Deviation for quantitative. The findings revealed that family expectations, spousal approval, community norms, religious beliefs, and fear of social criticism significantly constrain women’s entry into and growth of businesses. Despite these barriers, women adopt coping strategies such as operating home-based enterprises, seeking family support, networking with other women, and selecting socially acceptable business sectors. The study concludes that socio-cultural barriers remain a major determinant of low female entrepreneurial engagement in Nigeria. It is recommended that cultural reorientation programs, family support initiatives, stronger women’s networks, and gender-sensitive business training be implemented to enhance women’s participation in entrepreneurship and contribute meaningfully to economic development.

oa:W7216703587.title: EXISTENCE, FAITH, AND THE ABSURD: RELIGIOUS AND METAPHYSICAL REFLECTIONS IN CHEKHOV’S META-THEATRICAL PLAYS
oa:W7216703587.venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Religion
oa:W7216703587.abstract: With the global spread of Chekhov’s plays in the 20th century, his works have transcended their literary origins to become foundational texts in modern theatre, influencing both dramatic realism and avant-garde experimentation. Beyond their structural and thematic innovations, Chekhov’s plays engage deeply with existential, metaphysical, and spiritual questions, making them fertile ground for religious and philosophical inquiry. His dramatic texts possess a meta-theatrical quality, not only reflecting the human condition but also serving as a medium for grappling with themes of faith, meaning, and transcendence. This study examines Chekhov’s plays as philosophical theatre, exploring how they resonate with religious and metaphysical thought in their engagement with fate, suffering, and the search for purpose. Through an analysis of theatrical interpretations—including Stanislavsky’s psychological realism, the metaphysical dimensions in productions by the Koriada Theater, Red Torch Theater, and Alexander Linski Theater—this research reveals how Chekhov’s works have been adapted to reflect contemporary existential and spiritual concerns. His dramas often evoke a sense of waiting, disillusionment, and silent prayer, mirroring theological reflections on divine silence, existential uncertainty, and the search for redemption in a seemingly indifferent world. By examining the interplay between theatrical realism, meta-theatrical awareness, and philosophical reflection, this study highlights Chekhov’s enduring influence as a dramatist whose works not only depict reality but also invite meditations on the sacred, the absurd, and the metaphysical. This research contributes to the broader discourse on religious philosophy and dramatic arts, arguing that Chekhov’s theatre functions

oa:W7216833354.title: The Vulnerability of Theology
oa:W7216833354.abstract: In the modern era, theology has been restricted to religious life. Instead, it should take God as its subject matter and resist the gerrymandering that has been urged on it. Julian of Norwich points the way forward to consider how theology ought to concern all things as well as how it should negotiate the differences that come about when theology primarily concerns God hidden and God crucified.

oa:W7217022576.title: DIVINE HIDDENNESS AND HUMAN REASON: EXPLORING THE EPISTEMOLOGICAL CHALLENGES IN CONTEMPORARY THEISM
oa:W7217022576.venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Religion
oa:W7217022576.abstract: The idea of divine hiddenness looks for why there is no evident and unequivocal evidence of God's existence and seeks to answer these questions within the philosophy of religion. Those who criticize complain that if all things are being done well, he would be conspicuously displayed; the existence of these honest unbelievers indicates a lack of care or no such thing at all. To this, theists reply that divine hiddenness has needful purposes, e.g., keeping free will, provoking true faith, and facilitating moral and spiritual perfection growth. This paper analyses the arguments for and against divine hiddenness concerning the consequences of belief, faith, and human reasoning. The discussion suggests the subtle relationship between divine presence and human perception, which is a key issue in religious epistemology. The process of faith and reason continues to be a battle that the current theism faces, thus causing epistemological challenges. Recent theories of arguments for God's existence have come under scrutiny, but rationalist theists continue to elaborate philosophical counter-arguments. Divine hiddenness, the problem of evil, and the nature of religious experience are the issues that contribute to the discourse, which requires a proper balance between theological commitment and philosophical inquiry. Ultimately, though, this process of enquiring into epistemic justification in theism continues to be a dialogue stemming from humanity and how human beings understand and believe.

oa:W7217041150.title: ҚАЗАҚ ДАЛАСЫНДАҒЫ ИШАНДАР МЕН МОЛДАЛАР ЖӘНЕ ОЛАРДЫҢ КЕҢЕС ӨКІМЕТІ ТАРАПЫНАН ҚУДАЛАУҒА ҰШЫРАУЫ
oa:W7217041150.venue: Habaršy. Tarih ža̋ne saâsi-a̋leumettìk ġylymdar seriâsy
oa:W7217041150.abstract: In this work, the role of ishans and mullahs in the religious and social life of the Kazakh steppe in the pre-Soviet and early years is considered, as well as the policy of persecution of priests by the Soviet authorities is analyzed. At the beginning of the twentieth century, ishans and mullahs played a key role in the spread of Islam among Kazakhs, as well as were important figures in the organization of public life, education and culture. However, with the establishment of Soviet power, an active campaign was launched to abolish religious institutions, which also affected the Muslim clergy. The Soviet authorities promoted atheism and organized repressions against the ishans and mullahs, demanding the abolition of all religious manifestations. These actions included arrest, deportation, shooting, and other forms of violence. As a result, a significant number of religious leaders were destroyed or forced to emigrate. Repression led to the destruction of the traditional religious structure and profound changes in the life of the Kazakh people. The work also analyzed the consequences of this persecution for Kazakh society, culture and religious practice and stressed the importance of studying this period in order to understand the historical context of religious and social changes in Kazakhstan in the twentieth century.

oa:W7217044731.title: Literasi Ekonomi Islam, Religiusitas, dan Intensi Transaksi E-Commerce: Peran Mediasi Sikap Konsumen Muslim
oa:W7217044731.abstract: Researching how Muslims make purchases online is becoming more important as e-commerce in Indonesia continues to expand. The purpose of this study is to analyze the influence of Islamic economic literacy and religious values on the intention to engage in e-commerce transactions, with Muslim consumer attitudes serving as a mediating variable, among Gen Z students at Jombang University. The studies strategy used in this studies is a survey-based quantitative technique. In order to gather data, 96 individuals were chosen using a purposive sample method and given a Likert-scale questionnaire. With the help of the SmartPLS 4.0 tool, the studies data was analyzed utilizing PLS-SEM technique. The results demonstrate that religious beliefs and Islamic economic literacy positively affect the propensity to engage in online business. The impact of Islamic economic literacy and religious beliefs on transaction intentions was shown to be mediated by Muslim consumer attitudes. Also, e-commerce purchase intent is positively impacted by Muslim customer views. Students' favorable views and intents to transact via e-commerce platforms that conform with Sharia rules may be strengthened by strengthening their Islamic economic literacy and religiosity, according to this research. Universities, e-commerce operators, and other relevant organizations should prioritize Islamic economic literacy instruction and work to develop religious values in order to promote digital transaction behavior that is in line with Sharia standards, according to the implications of this study

oa:W7217122700.title: Kampen om mælken
oa:W7217122700.abstract: Den danske konkurrencelov er i bund og grund god nok. Den er inden for de sidste fem år blevet harmoniseret med EU's konkurrencelovgivning så erhvervslivet kun skal arbejde under ét sæt konkurrenceregler Konkurrenceloven (KL) er en rammelov, der overlader det til konkurrencemyndighederne at vurdere, om en given adfærd udgør et konkurrencepolitisk problem. Sådanne vurderinger må i langt de fleste sager bygge på en industriøkonomisk analyse af kilden til konkurrencebegrænsningen. I forbindelse med behandlingen af konkurrenceproblemer mejerisektoren, har Konkurrenceråd (KR) og -styrelse (KS) i en række sager forsøgt at begrænse barrierer for potentiel konkurrence god overensstemmelse med moderne industriøkonomi for kooperativer Disse beslutninger er imidlertid blevet underkendt af Konkurrenceankenævnet (KA), oftest med en meget uklar og/eller kortfattet argumentation Det har undermineret den måde KL praktiseres på i mejerisektoren. Der er dermed skabt behov for en præcisering af forholdet mellem andelsretten og KL.

oa:W7217204382.title: Relevansi Konsep Akidah Imam Al-Ghazali dalam Al-Iqtishad Fi Al-I'tiqad terhadap Pendidikan Agama Islam
oa:W7217204382.abstract: Social media has reached people across all boundaries. This makes it easier for them to communicate without barriers. On the one hand, this convenience has positive effects; on the other hand, it has negative consequences. In Islamic teachings, Al-Ghazali authored a work on creed that teaches moderation in matters of faith, namely the book Al-Iqtishad fi Al-I’tiqad. Thus, this book is relevant to the aforementioned issue. Therefore, the focus of this study is on the concept of faith in Al-Iqtishad fi Al-I’tiqad and how this concept relates to Islamic Religious Education. This is a qualitative study in the form of library research employing content analysis. The results of this study show that the concept of faith presented in the book Al-Iqtishad fi Al-I’tiqad is a faith based primarily on sharia evidence (dalil syariat) or revealed evidence (dalil naqli), supplemented by rational evidence (dalil aqli) to reinforce the sharia evidence. This faith centers on three main topics. First, regarding the proof of God’s existence, His having no beginning, His eternity, the fact that God’s form is not a substance (jauhar), a body (jism), or an accident (aradl), God’s visibility, and His oneness. Second, regarding the seven attributes of God, namely power (qudrah), knowledge (ilm), life (hayah), will (irodah), hearing (sama’), sight (bashar), and speech (kalam). These seven attributes are distinct from Allah’s essence; although distinct, all these attributes are inherent in that essence. All these attributes are eternal, including the names derived from them and their corresponding actions. oa:W7217248049.title: MAINSTREAM CHRISTIAN CHURCHES AND SEXUAL DIVERSITY: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF ATTITUDES, PRACTICES, AND INCLUSION OF GAY AND LESBIAN COMMUNITIES
authors: Ramohlale P.P, Chauke O.R, Ramogale P and Ramohlale M.I.
oa:W7217248049.abstract: Mainstream Christian churches are long-established and institutionally recognised denominations that have played a significant role in shaping religious beliefs and practices in South Africa. These include the Roman Catholic, Anglican, Methodist, Lutheran, and Presbyterian churches. This study critically examines the attitudes, practices, and approaches of these churches towards lesbian and gay communities within the context of South Africa's constitutional commitment to equality and non-discrimination. A qualitative research approach, guided by a case study design, was employed to explore the perspectives and experiences of church leaders and congregants. Data were collected through focus group discussions and document analysis. The findings indicate that mainstream Christian churches continue to grapple with the challenges posed by sexual diversity, particularly regarding the recognition and blessing of same-sex marriages, the participation of lesbian and gay individuals in church leadership and worship, and the acceptance of diverse gender expression. These issues reflect the broader tension between adherence to traditional theological doctrines and the demands of an inclusive constitutional democracy. The study concludes that mainstream Christian churches remain engaged in an ongoing process of negotiating the balance between preserving doctrinal integrity and responding to evolving societal expectations for inclusion and equal treatment of lesbian and gay communities.

oa:W7217299554.title: Logos ukryty: rāzā jako hermeneutyka Słowa w poezji Efrema Syryjczyka
oa:W7217299554.abstract: The article interprets the Syriac concept rāzā (ܪܳ ܳܙܳܐ) as a hermeneutical key in the poetry of Ephrem the Syrian. In his thought, rāzā denotes the way the Logos dwells in the world without ceasing to be God – the presence of the divine in the visible. It expresses a structure of revelation grounded in the tension between the hidden and the revealed, disclosing a single logic of the Word’s activity in creation, Scripture, and the Incarnation. In these dimensions, the symbol becomes a locus of God’s real yet hidden presence, unveiling his mystery through the veil of signs, words, and flesh.

oa:W7217429833.title: Dane osobowe ujawniające przekonania religijne w kontekście prawa do bycia zapomnianym (art. 17 RODO) w Polsce
oa:W7217429833.abstract: The problem addressed: The tension between the right to be forgotten (GDPR art. 17) and the autonomy of religious associations in processing personal data revealing religious beliefs, with particular reference to the Catholic Church in Poland. The aim of the research conducted: To examine the legal relationship between the right to privacy and the right to religious freedom under Polish and European law, and to assess the scope and limits of the right to be forgotten in the context of church data processing. Methods: Doctrinal-legal method of interpretation, supported by analysis of case law and supervisory practice. The results of the research: The article identifies the specifics of data processing regulations within the Catholic Church in Poland, clarifies the legal and supervisory practice context, and establishes the significance of the exception provided by Article 91 GDPR concerning the autonomy of religious associations in the realm of data protection. The conclusions drawn from the research: The right to be forgotten is not absolute; its application in the religious context must take into account constitutional frameworks, the specificity of canon law, and the need to balance individual rights with the institutional rights of religious communities.

oa:W766712332.title: C. S. Lewis on the Problem of Divine Hiddenness
oa:W766712332.abstract: Along with the problem of evil, the problem of divine hiddenness has become one of the most prominent arguments for atheism in the contemporary philosophy of religion. Roughly it is this: if there is a loving God, surely he would make his existence apparent to us, and in a way that we could not rationally doubt. Why? (i) Because it is of the nature of love that the lover will seek open relationship with the object of love, and (ii) because on most traditional theisms it is claimed that our ultimate well-being requires having a positive relationship with God, which relationship presupposes belief in God's reality. Yet as a matter of fact many people fail to believe in God, and that through no fault of their own. Such nonbelief is incompatible with the truth of theism. Therefore God does not exist. Here I explore how the writings of C. S. Lewis (probably the twentieth century's most popular Anglican author) can be brought to bear on the problem.

oa:W796406606.title: Speaking from the Gaps: The Eloquent Silence of God in Esther
oa:W796406606.abstract: Of all the books of the Hebrew Bible, the book of Esther presents the most consistently silent God. God's silence in the book seems to fall into Korpel and De Moor's category of 'incomprehensible divine silence'. Silent though God may be in the book of Esther, it does not necessarily imply a complete absence of the divine person or of faith. In the book, the author's use of intertextual allusions extends both to details within the book itself and to texts from other books of the Hebrew Bible. The wealth of intertextual links between the book on the one hand and texts that explicitly speak of God as both acting and speaking on the other is vast. In accordance with the emphasis on human freedom, it leaves more room for God's sovereign choice to speak or not to speak than other books of the Hebrew Bible do. Keywords: book of Esther; De Moore; eloquent silence; God; Hebrew Bible; Korpel

oa:W833996755.title: ‘It Shall Be Night to You, without Vision’: The Theme of Divine Disfavour in the Biblical Prophetic Books
oa:W833996755.abstract: This chapter deals with the theme of God's silence, his alienation and withdrawal from his people, as found in the Biblical prophetic books, against the background of the theme of divine disfavour in the Ancient Near East. Korpel and De Moor make clear that the imagery of Gods as 'speaking' or 'being silent' in the texts from the ancient world, is modelled on the speaking and silence of humans. The examples that Korpel and De Moor present of divine silence are not really convincing. The motif of broken communication, because of God's anger with his people, is prominent in the book of Jeremiah. Broken communication because of divine anger is strongly present in the book of Ezekiel. Divine silence and abandonment are symptomatic of divine anger. Both in his speaking and in his silence, God acts according to his own divine plan, which is a mystery to humans. Keywords: Biblical prophetic books; De Moor; divine anger; divine disfavour; divine silence; Ezekiel; Jeremiah; Korpel

oa:W83539168.title: "JHWH, Gott der Rettung" und das Schreien aus "finsterem Ort" : Klangmuster und andere Stilmittel in Psalm 88
oa:W83539168.abstract: A structural analysis of Ps 88 serves as a point of departure for a study of the poetics and especially the sound patterns and other stylistic figures that characterize the psalm. The ways in which sonic figures can serve to counter traumatic need in the psalm are discussed. The vocative expression in the opening line, 'Yhwh, God of my salvation!', already marks an important moment in this process. Because of the divine silence, dialogue does not take place. And yet, the situation is expressed via details of the psalm's structure, including the alternating sonic expressions of first and second person suffixes. Viewed as a whole, there is a progressive descent from the opening exclamation to the dismayed and powerlessly whispered conclusion in which 'a dark place' occupies the foreground.

oa:W893288475.title: Ex Oriente Silentium: An Introduction to This Volume
oa:W893288475.abstract: This chapter deals with the theme of the Divine Silence. Divine Silence is an expression of the uncomprehended and incomprehensible laceration and fragmentation of the human existence. It is no proof of divine absence. The author agrees with Korpel and De Moor, when they state that all language about God has a metaphorical character. Korpel and De Moor correctly locate 'silence' in the context of 'speaking'. Fear for divine silence can be seen as a background for various Mesopotamian prayers. Korpel and De Moor make more than clear that the concept of divine silence as means of communication is not to be seen as only an idea from contemporary culture, but has deep roots in antiquity and beyond. Silence gives voice to something otherwise incommunicable. The choice for a strategy for communication does not seem to be dependent on human speaking or silence. Keywords: De Moor; Divine Silence; God; Korpel

oa:W899058945.title: Divine Silence or Divine Absence? Converging Metaphors in Family Religion in Ancient Israel and the Levant
oa:W899058945.abstract: This chapter demonstrates the family religion's concern for maintaining favorable divine-human relationships translated into a concern over divine absence or silence in connection with birth, daily life, and death. Korpel and de Moor draw a distinction between divine silence and divine absence, noting absent deity does not speak because he is not there to enter into a dialogue, whereas a silent deity can be attentively listening or may have reason to keep silent. Divine speech appears as an explicit concern among personal names from ancient Israel and the broader Levant. The family based religious settings are distinguished from the public socio-religious sphere of temples at city, regional, and supra-regional levels. Even if the dead cannot praise Israel's God in death, the loving and grieving family can do so on behalf of its deceased in hopes that one may at least hear a divine response in the place of silence. Keywords: de Moor; divine absence; divine silence; family religion; Israel; Korpel; Levant

oa:W924337676.title: How Comprehensible Can Divine Silence Be? Reflections on the Biblical Evidence
oa:W924337676.abstract: The Silent God deals with the theme of divine silence. The distinction between comprehensible and incomprehensible silence of God is noteworthy. Humans may find the lack of communication as problematic. The reasons for the silence of the Gods are there in the texts. Korpel and De Moor indicate that in certain situations prophecy and other means to learn the will of God were absent or scarce, especially when God was angry. The Bible contains many explicit and implicit warnings against imprudent speaking in the name of God. Walter Brueggemann wants to do justice to the theological diversity in the Hebrew Bible and distinguishes biblical 'core testimony' from biblical 'counter-testimony'. In Qohelet God acts, but he does not speak and his acts are incomprehensible. The modern attention for the silence of God has ancient roots, in the Bible and in ancient Near Eastern texts that are much older than the Bible. Keywords: Biblical evidence; De Moor; divine silence; Korpel; Qohelet; Walter Brueggemann

oa:W93586732.title: Introduction: The Hiddenness of God
oa:W93586732.abstract: Many people are perplexed, even troubled, by the fact that God (if such there be) has not made His existence sufficiently clear. This fact – the fact of divine hiddenness – is a source of existential concern for many people. That is, it raises problems about their very existence, particularly its value and purpose. The fact of divine hiddenness is also, according to some people, a source of good evidence against the existence of God. That is, it allegedly poses a cognitive problem for theism, in the form of evidence challenging the assumption that God exists. (Here and throughout we speak of “God” as broadly represented in the historic Jewish and Christian theistic traditions.) Existential Concern The existential problem often takes the form of a crisis of faith, sometimes leading to a collapse of trust in God. Jewish and Christian theists have committed themselves to the God who, they believe, loves them perfectly. They expect to find their greatest good, their ultimate fulfillment, in personal and social relationship with God. In the Jewish tradition, this general idea finds elaboration in God's entering into a covenant relationship with the people of Israel, who are to respond to God in faithful obedience. In the Christian tradition, the idea sometimes takes a more individualistic turn. To be sure, God enters into covenant relationship with a “people” – namely, the Church inaugurated by Jesus Christ – but Christians often emphasize the importance of each person's entering into a personal relationship with God through Jesus Christ. There are, of course, differences in interpretation and emphasis between and within the distinctive traditions of Judaism and Christianity.
